subcomponents.title: Presentation code and tests

criteria.rationale: The sample's presentation.css and the presentation template's presentation.css use only unscoped selectors. Examples are [data-presentation-box], [data-presentation-attribution], [data-presentation-toc-entry] and [data-presentation-arrow] path. [data-presentation-root] is the kit's root on every presentation, so it is not a root class or hook owned by this presentation. These rules would leak to other presentations after client-side navigation. It is not a CSS module.

criteria.rationale: The props are typed from the rendered element (NodeProps from HTMLMotionProps<'div'>), and kit-only props such as Icon, symbol and entering are stripped. But the kit's identity hooks are set before the caller's props are spread. Box renders data-presentation-box before {...props}, Label/Frame/Emphasis do the same, SymbolChip puts data-presentation-chip and data-presentation-symbol before {...props}, Arrow puts data-presentation-arrow before {...rest}, and SceneLayer puts data-presentation-layer before {...rest}. A caller can therefore override these hooks, so the second clause fails.

criteria.rationale: The requirement is that browser-driving tests wait for observable state before asserting and use no fixed sleeps. The delivered tests drive Chromium only by running the verify and inspect scripts, and that browser automation sleeps for a fixed time before collecting the state the tests assert on. In scripts/verify.mjs, renderEveryStep waits for the step index and then calls page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS), a fixed 1800 ms. Only after that does it read the title, caption and errors that the E2E test asserts on (the outline/render pass, 'VERIFY FAILED [outline] (step 1)', and the late-fault step attribution). The bootstrap inspect helper that tests/integration/inspection.integration.test.ts runs calls page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) before collecting the diagnostics and screenshot behind each asserted warning. The test also asserts that captures are at least 1800 ms apart, a result only a fixed sleep produces. The kit exposes no settled signal for the scripts to poll. So the 'no fixed sleeps / wait for observable state' clause is unmet. This rules with Judge C. Judge A is right that the test files themselves contain no sleep calls and that the scripts poll data-step-index. That does not decide the requirement: the scripts are the browser-driving code these tests execute, they add a fixed sleep after that poll before the asserted state is read, and the integration test checks that this sleep happened. Judge B's evidence covers jsdom component tests (sample.test.tsx, presentation.test.tsx, router.test.tsx), which use waitFor/findBy and do not drive a browser. It also cites the spawnSync-based E2E test without looking at the fixed waitForTimeout inside the verify run that test drives. Clean jsdom tests cannot cancel out a browser test path that sleeps.

subcomponents.title: Verified candidate-produced testing evidence

criteria.rationale: The only verified, usable record is a diff-scoped round-1 retest. It covers the step-6 tray frame, the step-4 and step-9 cascade regression, and the 390px fit at steps 8 and 9. The log says it did not repeat the earlier coverage floor and lists as 'Deliberately not exercised' the sample steps, the keyboard and touch matrices, the skill workflows, the route and error journeys, the helper and the verification workflow. That is a disclosed omission, but the reason is the pass's chosen scope, not an environmental impediment, so it counts against coverage. The round-0 screenshots in the packet have no capture metadata and no recorded observation, so they cannot stand in for coverage. Most scenarios in the approved specs have no verified observation: present/browse mode, navigation, boundary clamping, morph/enter/exit sequencing, attribution, the scaffold, create/modify, and verification pass/fail. A substantial share of the behavior is therefore unexercised.

It also says the bootstrap starter 'builds and renders' with browser-default styling, which maps to the scaffold and quality-bar scenarios. subcomponents.title: Observable assumption handling

criteria.rationale: The omission check found no unsurfaced deviation. The two deviations the record reproduced were both surfaced. The tray frame at step 6 (F-001) was logged as a defect, fixed and retested. Unreadable diagram text at 390px (F-002) was logged as an open decision with options and consequences. The ledger also raises two further gaps the tester saw: departing-entity motion cannot be shown by the accumulate-only sample, and the bootstrap starter is unstyled. It also records many spec ambiguities, such as attribution URL, swipe threshold, and the 'dense step' definition. I found no deviation in the log or findings that the ledger leaves out.

F-002 entry lists options 1–4, each with a stated consequence, and marks the user decision as pending.

judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The ledger separates repository facts from inference. The attribution URL is taken from the repo's origin remote. The design and CLAUDE.md are cited for the data-presentation prefix, the byte-parity rule, and the no-CI rule. Observations are kept apart from rulings. The reproduced F-001 violation was treated as a defect and fixed, not called acceptable. The reproduced F-002 gap was left open as a decision with the 'accept the limitation' option and its consequence stated, which the guidance allows. I found no misstated fact. The bare starter is correctly tied to the scaffold-neutrality requirement.

criteria.rationale: The candidate decided routine spec gaps itself and recorded each with a rationale and 'Pending: none'. Examples are the swipe threshold, the aria-current values, and the overlap marker name. It escalated only the decisions that would change approved behavior: F-002 (the canvas or no-reflow model), departing-entity coverage, and starter styling. It did not apply a partial fix that would hide F-002. It fixed F-001 directly because the requirement is explicit. No reproduced violation was labelled acceptable, and the candidate took no decision it lacked authority for.

criteria.rationale: The only handoff in the packet is the gate notice. It gives two reasons: the tester's status was NOT_READY, and acceptance-handoff.md was missing or empty. votes.rationale: startPreview reserves an ephemeral port, closes the probe server, and spawns vite preview with --strictPort. Readiness is decided only by HTTP polling of that URL in waitUntilServing. The child's exit is checked via child.exitCode only at the top of each loop iteration, before the fetch. Nothing parses the child's own announcement of its address, and the child's exit is not raced against readiness. If another process takes the released port, the strict-port child exits, but that process's response can satisfy fetch before the exit is observed, so a non-owned server is accepted. Neither credited mechanism is implemented.
evidence: scripts/lib/preview.mjs freePort: server.close then resolve(port), so the port is released before vite starts
scripts/lib/preview.mjs startPreview spawn uses stdio ['ignore','ignore','pipe']; stderr is only buffered for error messages, never parsed for readiness
scripts/lib/preview.mjs waitUntilServing: `if (child.exitCode !== null) throw` is sampled before each fetch, and `if (response.ok) return` accepts any responder

votes.rationale: The verifier reserves a free port, but readiness comes from HTTP polling of that port, not from the child's own announcement. The only ownership check is child.exitCode sampled before each fetch. Any server already answering on the port is accepted as ready before the child's exit is seen, and --strictPort alone is not enough. Neither credited mechanism is present.
evidence: scripts/lib/preview.mjs waitUntilServing(): each loop checks `if (child.exitCode !== null) throw`, then `fetch(url)`, and returns when `response.ok`.

The test also asserts that captures are at least 1800 ms apart, a result only a fixed sleep produces. The kit exposes no settled signal for the scripts to poll. scene-kit.rationale: The newcomer path and the continuing path are separate in the source. In entryMotion.ts, entering=true gives initial opacity 0 and a transition with delay ENTER_DELAY (0.7). entering=false gives initial:false and a transition with no delay, using LAYOUT_T (0.6). Since 0.7 >= 0.6, a newcomer's visible entry starts after the continuing layout transition ends. The delay applies only to the newcomer element. NodeBase and Arrow both spread entryMotion(entering). Label, SymbolChip, Frame, Emphasis and Box all wrap NodeBase and forward props, so `entering` reaches it. In SampleScene, `entering` is the set of ids absent from the previous step's ids. renderEntity passes it through entryAttributes to every identified entity. That covers Box, Label, SymbolChip, Frame and Arrow, and the default branch goes through renderArrow, which also passes it. Nested parts (card title/caption/visual, verify label, pass chip, frame caption) have no identity of their own and sit inside an identified parent that starts at opacity 0. They are structural children, not entities. No sample entity renders without entry motion.

Every imported symbol is used, so noUnusedLocals passes. - **steps.ts** builds Step<SceneState> objects with id, era, title, caption, Scene, payload and groupKey, which are exactly the fields in the kit's Step interface. It imports './beats', './entities', './Scene' and './payload', all present in the template folder. - **beats.ts** types `enter` as BoxId|ArrowId from './entities', and its values start, middle, end, first, second match the keys in BOXES and ARROWS. - **payload.ts** defines SceneState and SceneEntity from EntityId. **entities.ts** exports BOXES, ARROWS, layoutIdFor, rectStyle and the id types, with only the slug placeholders to substitute. - **Talk.tsx** passes `steps`, `title` and `initialMode`, which are valid PresentationProps. The same test asserts the materialized kit is byte-identical to the canonical src/presentation-kit. The tsconfig settings (verbatimModuleSyntax, erasableSyntaxOnly, noUnusedLocals) are satisfied, because type imports use `type`, there are no enums, and no import is unused.

It requires a non-zero exit at a check that reports the sample as missing or not matching the outline. It also says a failure that only shows up later as a render timeout fails the criterion. If the registered sample has no steps, Presentation returns null when steps[nav.index] is undefined. The section that carries data-step-count therefore never mounts. Because no step-0 runtime error is recorded, waitForSelector('[data-step-count]', 15_000) times out. The catch block then throws VerifyFailure('render', 'the presentation chrome did not appear ...: <timeout message>'). That is the render-timeout path the guidance rules out, not a sample or outline check. This scenario comes straight from the guidance's definition of a missing sample. It is not a partial-deletion scenario such as removing an imported file while its import remains. The e2e cases cover only a renamed slug ([sample]) and reordered steps ([outline]). Neither one covers absent steps content.

first_results.rationale: The requirement is that browser-driving tests wait for observable state before asserting and use no fixed sleeps. The delivered tests drive Chromium only by running the verify and inspect scripts, and that browser automation sleeps for a fixed time before collecting the state the tests assert on. In scripts/verify.mjs, renderEveryStep waits for the step index and then calls page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS), a fixed 1800 ms. Only after that does it read the title, caption and errors that the E2E test asserts on (the outline/render pass, 'VERIFY FAILED [outline] (step 1)', and the late-fault step attribution). The bootstrap inspect helper that tests/integration/inspection.integration.test.ts runs calls page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) before collecting the diagnostics and screenshot behind each asserted warning. The test also asserts that captures are at least 1800 ms apart, a result only a fixed sleep produces. The kit exposes no settled signal for the scripts to poll. So the 'no fixed sleeps / wait for observable state' clause is unmet. This rules with Judge C. Judge A is right that the test files themselves contain no sleep calls and that the scripts poll data-step-index. That does not decide the requirement: the scripts are the browser-driving code these tests execute, they add a fixed sleep after that poll before the asserted state is read, and the integration test checks that this sleep happened. Judge B's evidence covers jsdom component tests (sample.test.tsx, presentation.test.tsx, router.test.tsx), which use waitFor/findBy and do not drive a browser. It also cites the spawnSync-based E2E test without looking at the fixed waitForTimeout inside the verify run that test drives. Clean jsdom tests cannot cancel out a browser test path that sleeps.

Then they call page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS = 1800) or page.waitForTimeout(options.settleMs) before reading the title, caption, errors, diagnostics and screenshot that the tests assert on. That is a fixed-millisecond wait for a transition, used in place of waiting on a settled state. - **The integration test depends on the sleep.** Lines 53-58 assert that captures are at least 1800 ms apart, so the test only passes if the fixed sleep happens. - **No other criterion covers this.** No other engineering-quality criterion names this defect, so scoring it here does not count it twice. - **The noise rule does not apply.** That rule only says no credit is given, and no fail is given, for missing *longer* settle delays. It does not excuse having fixed sleeps. The test files contain no sleep calls of their own, and the scripts do poll the step index. Neither point helps, because the requirement forbids any fixed sleep in the browser-driving path that the tests run and assert on.

engineering-quality.rationale: The auditor's claim does not hold. The guidance fails this criterion only when a readiness wait has no timeout. Both preview.mjs copies do give the readiness wait a timeout. waitUntilServing sets a deadline from timeoutMs (30,000 ms by default) and loops only while that deadline has not passed. It also stops early if the child process exits, and it throws a timeout error when the deadline expires. The auditor's case needs a single fetch to a loopback vite preview server to hang. Nothing in the material shows that happening. A connection to a port with no listener is refused at once, and Node's built-in fetch has its own default timeouts. So this is a hypothetical input that the review guidance does not name, and it does not defeat the pass. The other two clauses also hold. In verify and inspect, the build runs to completion through spawnSync before startPreview is called. Readiness comes from HTTP polling, and the preview's stdout is ignored, so the ready-URL parsing clause does not apply.
